newsitem.title: USA: US Mint gains authority for platinum, gold coins.
newsitem.headline: US Mint gains authority for platinum, gold coins.

text.p: The U.S. Mint has authority, as part of the fiscal 1997 budget which took effect Tuesday, to issue a platinum coin and a second type of gold coin.
A spokesman said it was premature to discuss the Mint's plans on the coins.
The Mint already sells the American Eagle gold coin.
Under language in the fiscal 1997 funding law, the Mint could use U.S. government stockpiles of platinum as working inventory to produce platinum coins. The reserves would have to be replenished.
A separate provision requires profits from the sale of gold coins be deposited into the Treasury's general funds.

For commemorative coins, Treasury after Jan 1, 1999, would have authority to issue coins under no more than two commemorative programs, according to the funding law. It would be limited to not more than 750,000 "clad" half-dollar coins, not more than 500,000 silver one-dollar coins and not more than 100,000 gold five-dollar and 10-dollar coins.
